messages:
alex: noticing gradual GPU mem growth on long KV-cache runs — not immediate OOM but resident grows ~200MB every 6h for a few nodes. no obvious alloc spikes in trace, but nvprof snapshots show lots of small cudaMallocs around cache churn.
priya: ugh. could be fragmentation OR orphaned buffers. does it correlate with sequence-length spikes or batching changes? any recent kernel-picker changes?
alex: timeline: rolled kernel-picker perf patch two days ago; also enabled adaptive-batching experimental flag last week. growth started after the kernel change. seq len distribution hasn't changed much.
marco: can you paste the profiler snapshot id? also we should run the micro repro that toggles KV cache insert/delete patterns. fragmentation repro helps separate true leak vs allocator churn.
alex: snapshot: https://internal-artifacts/reports/nvprof/1779123401-snap.png (shows lots of 16k/32k allocs). attaching short run log: 
```
2026-03-10T09:12:00Z INFO start kv-bench --threads=8 --max-seq=2048 --ops=1e7
2026-03-10T15:12:00Z INFO end kv-bench resident=14230MB -> 14450MB
```
carol: the allocator we use (redwood-cuda-alloc v2) tries to keep free pools for quick reuse; if we changed kernel selection it might change workspace sizing leading to more pools. Try lowering `allocator.workspace_max_mb` on a canary host to 128 and enable `reuse_buffers=true`.
priya: +1 to change workspace cap. also add `--dump-alloc-stats` to the runtime and collect after 1h intervals (`/debug/alloc_stats`). that will show outstanding chunks per size class.
marco: here's a minimal repro you can run on a dev GPU to emulate churn: 
```
python util/kv_repro.py --insert-rate=500 --delete-rate=450 --key-size=64 --value-size=8192 --duration=2h
# repro toggles between short/long seqs every 10k ops
```
run with `USE_REUSE=0` then `USE_REUSE=1` to compare.
infra-bot: alert: OOM-trend detected on cluster-rw-gpu-12 (p95 memory delta > 10% over 24h) :warning:
sre_lead: let's schedule a quick canary job. alex, carve out one node and run marco's repro with the runtime flags Carol suggested. collect `/debug/alloc_stats`, nvprof, and an `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` snapshot every 30m.
alex: will run now. starting with workspace_max_mb=128 reuse_buffers=true. launching repro with `--dump-alloc-stats` every 30m. posting logs when available. :thumbsup:
priya: if the alloc_stats show long-lived free blocks across many size classes -> fragmentation. if they show constantly growing in-use counters -> true leak (unfreed handles). either way we should add a test in perf CI that runs KV churn for 2h and compares resident delta.
carol: note: kernel-picker change also introduced extra temporary buffers for fused attention in some code paths. add a quick patch to free temporaries immediately in the fused path as a canary. if that flattens growth it's likely transient buffers not reclaimed.
marco: nice. also try toggling `batching.max_prefetch_tokens=0` to avoid speculative workspace grabs. that helped on a similar issue last quarter.
alex: first 1h results posted: resident 14230MB -> 14300MB, alloc_stats show increased free-chunks in 32k and 64k classes with total free pool growing. nvprof still shows many small allocs. looks like fragmentation + larger free pools.
sre_lead: preliminary conclusion: allocator pool growth triggered by kernel/pathway change + adaptive batching prefetching. mitigation path: temp free in fused path + reduce workspace cap + enable buffer reuse. prioritize a rollback of kernel-picker if canary doesn't stabilize in next 12h.
priya: filing perf ticket with logs and repro command: PERF-2026-84. tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml.
alex: thanks — will keep thread updated with 6h/12h snapshots.
